github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/cmd/ch.summary: Offline drift sentry: compares the upstream versions pinned in pkg/versions against the npm registry's latest published release for each declared harness package. Prints a Markdown table or JSON and exits 0 when every pin matches, 1 on drift, and 2 when the pins could not be read or the registry could not be reached.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/cmd/fa.summary: A scriptable stand-in for an interactive coding harness, used by the PTY-driven integration tests. It reads a JSON script named by an environment variable, switches its PTY slave to raw mode like a real TUI, and replays the script's timeline of painted frames, input waits and exits. Not a product binary.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/cmd/ha.summary: HTTP + Server-Sent-Events gateway that exposes pkg/chat so non-Go clients can drive multi-turn harness conversations across a process boundary. It serves conversation, control-token, message, input, history and screen routes under /v1 and streams turn and input events as SSE frames. v1 ships no authentication and is meant to be bound to localhost.

The CLI front-end over pkg/wrapper and pkg/chat. It offers transparent PTY passthrough, a one-shot run that reads a prompt from stdin and prints the reply, a machine-readable structured-run that emits one turnproto JSON result line, and tmux-backed detached sessions with attach, status, kill and list subcommands. The dangerous sandbox-defaults injection is deliberately owned here, at the CLI boundary.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/docs/g.summary: The static-site generator for the documentation. It renders the canonical markdown under docs/md into themed HTML with syntax-highlighted code and inlined, theme-aware SVG diagrams, and can serve the built site locally for preview. It is a nested Go module so its rendering dependencies stay out of the main module's graph.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/intern.summary: The execution-environment core: a Provisioner axis for where the machine comes from, a Containment axis for what the agent may touch, the Workspace contract they meet at, the Compose combinator that joins them, and the lifecycle engine covering credential injection, redaction and retention. The model is batch request/response — exec, upload, download — with degenerate local and identity implementations shipped alongside the abstractions.

Acquirer.description: Optional, structurally-probed acquire hook of a Containment: acquires containment resources and returns a layer closed over them, cleaning up its own half-created resources on failure.

AliasMapper.description: Optional, structurally-probed host-URL rewrite of a ContainmentLayer, folded over the inner's for a two-hop alias.

Containment.description: Decides WHAT the agent may touch by contributing a ContainmentLayer of primitives that the core Compose combinator decorates a Workspace with.

ContainmentLayer.description: The set of primitives (exec wrap, path map, cross upload/download, teardown) a Containment contributes to the Compose combinator.

CredentialInjector.description: Applies secrets to a workspace, declares required capabilities and redactions, and cleans them up idempotently on destroy.

Provisioner.description: Decides WHERE the machine comes from: host-side preflight plus Create returning a Workspace for a WorkspaceSpec.

Redactor.description: Sink for secret strings to scrub from logs; the core registers every injector's redactions here before any Apply.

Workspace.description: An exec + file-transfer transport onto a machine: Exec, Upload/Download, path conventions, host-alias rewrite, and retention-honoring Destroy.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/intern.summary: The Daytona provisioner: elastically provisioned remote sandboxes exposed through the internal/env Workspace contract. It depends only on SDK interfaces declared locally rather than on the real Daytona SDK, so unit tests inject a fake and the live client is wired in only for the live test tier.

DaytonaSandbox.description: The subset of the real @daytonaio/sdk Sandbox surface this driver depends on: execute command, upload/download file, labels, id, and delete.

DaytonaSdkClient.description: The subset of the real @daytonaio/sdk Daytona client surface this driver depends on: Create a sandbox and List sandboxes matching a query.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/intern.summary: The OpenShell containment driver: a clean-room Go wrapper of the openshell CLI transport over env.Containment, with policy generation, host-alias rewrite, and deterministic sandbox naming.

The script format, fluent builder and one-time binary build behind the scriptable fake harness. It gives the chat tests a real program on a real PTY, so replays exercise the actual screen emulator, turn watcher and idle-completion timing that corpus replay alone cannot reach.

The terminal-emulator bake-off command. It replays each recorded scenario's raw PTY bytes through every registered emulator candidate and reports fidelity against the expected snapshot, stability after settling, and throughput — the measurement behind the project's vt100 emulator choice.

Records a live harness session under wrapper supervision, capturing the raw PTY byte stream and scenario metadata into a corpus directory. It runs interactively or unattended from a JSON script of wait, send, sleep and interrupt steps, bounded by an idle timeout and a maximum session duration.
CLI that generates a synthetic bake-off corpus exercising common TUI byte-stream primitives (SGR, cursor moves, alt-screen, box drawing) to validate bench plumbing.
Thin adapter interface around candidate vt100 emulator libraries so the bake-off harness can compare them on equal footing (feed bytes, read a text snapshot).

Emulator.description: Minimal bake-off surface over a vt100 emulator: Write raw PTY bytes, Snapshot the visible screen text, and report cursor position, size, and name.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/intern.summary: Comparison utilities for the screen-emulator bake-off: normalize, strip ANSI, exact match, and Levenshtein/normalized edit distance against ground-truth text.
Loads recorded bake-off scenarios from disk (bytes.raw + meta.json, optional expected.txt/transcript.jsonl) via Discover, Load, and WriteMeta.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/ch.summary: The Go chat-conversation API. Each Conversation owns one PTY-supervised harness process and exposes a FIFO control token, one assistant turn per Send, an event stream, request/answer handling for blocking prompts, transcript-backed history, and live permission-mode switching. Persistence is pluggable through the Store interface, and transports deliberately live outside this package.

Store.description: Persists chat-level session metadata and turn records (not transcript bodies); create/get/update sessions and append/update/list turns, safe for concurrent use.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/ch.summary: In-memory chat.Store implementation shipped with v1: holds sessions and turns in process memory, lost on restart; suitable for tests and single-process gateways.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/di.summary: Answers whether each harness declared in the version pins is installed on PATH and at what version, probing the binary's own version flag behind a cache keyed on binary path and modification time. It is read-only with respect to the system — it never installs, writes, or alters PATH — and treats 'not installed' and 'probe failed' as ordinary results rather than errors.

Probe.description: Parses a harness binary's version from its --version (or equivalent) output; cheap, one subprocess call, treating parse failures as errors.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/di.summary: A curated static registry of the model identifiers each harness accepts, plus a pure parser for the interactive model-picker screen. It is deliberately offline, because no supported harness exposes a machine-readable model list, so callers can validate or offer models without launching a CLI.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/en.summary: The public host-side client for running one structured turn inside a workspace. It uploads the prompt as a file so argv can never carry it, executes the structured-run runner in the guest, parses the last JSON line of stdout into a structured result, and optionally downloads the transcript. A non-zero guest exit is returned as a parsed result rather than an error.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/ha.summary: The per-harness orchestration and capability layer. Profiles resolve, once per run, which capabilities a harness actually offers — session-id extraction, resume arguments, stream parsing, hooks — while Run supervises a headless run and acquires its transcript through hooks or stream parsing, and RunTurn drives exactly one interactive turn on top of the chat layer. It is distinct from the TUI turn adapters under pkg/turns/harness.

HookProvider.description: The contract for a harness that can report events through its own hook mechanism: it declares the hook specification, installs that configuration into a worktree, and parses a hook subprocess's payload into transcript events.

Profile.description: A harness's capability descriptor. Resolve is called once per run with the concrete binary, arguments, environment and working directory, and returns only the capabilities confirmed for that run.

Resumer.description: Supplies the argument fragment that resumes an existing harness session for a given session id; an empty id yields no arguments.

SessionIDExtractor.description: Recovers the harness-assigned session UUID from a single line of the harness's headless stream output; stateless and idempotent per line.

StaticHookProfile.description: Optional Profile interface exposing the harness's static HookProvider so a fired-hook subprocess can obtain the payload parser without running Resolve.

StreamParser.description: Parses a single line of the harness's headless stream output into zero or more canonical events; stateless, idempotent, and tolerant of non-event lines.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/ha.summary: A side-effect-only package that blank-imports every built-in harness profile so that lookups by name resolve them. Callers who need just one harness may blank-import that subpackage instead.

The harness profile for the Claude Code CLI. It extracts the session id from Claude's machine-readable init event and supplies the resume argument prefix, with later capabilities covering stream parsing and hook installation. Importing the package registers the profile.
harness.Profile for the OpenAI Codex CLI: resume-only, since Codex's stream/hook/export contracts are under-documented and deliberately not implemented on a guess.
harness.Profile for the Gemini CLI: resume-by-id plus shell hooks in a Claude-shaped settings.json; hooks-only, with no stream parser until the schema is confirmed.
harness.Profile for the OpenCode CLI: resume + session-id only; no shell hooks (in-process plugins) and stream/export deferred until validatable.
harness.Profile for the pi coding agent: session-id, resume (--session), and a live --mode json stream parser validated against pi 0.76.0; no hooks (no shell-hook contract).

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/on.summary: The in-process library for running exactly one headless harness turn and classifying it into the frozen structured-turn status vocabulary. It owns the unattended policy — quit after the turn, auto-answer blocking prompts affirmatively, prefer the harness's own transcript for the reply — and returns every classified outcome with a nil error, reserving errors for unclassifiable failures.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/pr.summary: Single owner of the agent-profile contract: the .manifest.json launch-verification record, its fingerprint algorithm (sha256 over path + NUL + file bytes, in listed order, with harness_version compared separately rather than hashed), the per-harness config-root layout that decides what a provisioner copies versus what the harness owns at runtime, and the version-gated credential-slot rules as data. A pure translator — fs.FS in, values out — so a provisioner that writes and a supervisor that refuses to boot can share one implementation without either inheriting the other's side effects.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/sc.summary: Wraps a vt100 terminal emulator so a harness's raw PTY byte stream becomes queryable rendered state. It exposes writes, coherent point-in-time snapshots, a monotonic change generation, coalesced change subscriptions, and a resize that coordinates a fallible peer without holding the read lock.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/tr.summary: The read-only view of harness-owned session logs, together with the canonical harness-agnostic event model, its public and durable serializations, normalized token accounting, and the shared JSONL line helpers. It is a leaf package that imports neither the turns nor the chat layer, so anything may parse a harness log.

Reader.description: Reads a harness's persisted transcript for one session (by harness session UUID + working dir) into the canonical Event stream; safe for concurrent use.

UsageReader.description: An optional capability a transcript reader may also implement: best-effort token accounting for one session, returning nothing when the transcript carried no usage.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/tr.summary: Reads Claude Code's own JSONL session logs, locating a session by encoding the working directory into its projects path, and parses them into canonical transcript events plus optional token usage.

Reads Codex's rollout JSONL sessions from its date-partitioned sessions tree, parsing response-item envelopes into canonical transcript events and usage. It can also locate the most recent session for a working directory when no session id is known.
Reads Gemini CLI session transcripts (~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/chats/session-*.jsonl), accepting either observed line shape, into the canonical Event stream.

Reads pi's JSONL agent sessions, locating a session by working-directory slug with a directory-walk fallback and confirming the match against the in-file id header before parsing its typed content blocks.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/tu.summary: The neutral wire contract for one supervised turn: the status vocabulary, the canonical status-to-exit-code table, the frozen stderr deadline anchor, the structured result object, and the tolerant last-JSON-line parser hosts use to read it. Every exported name and JSON tag here is a frozen cross-repository contract.

Defines the per-harness adapter contract that turns screen snapshots and wrapper status into a small set of turn events, the optional capability interfaces an adapter may opt into, the model for interactive input requests, and the watcher that pumps a wrapper session and a screen into one event stream.

Adapter.description: Per-harness contract translating screen state and wrapper status into turn events; OnScreen/OnWrapperStatus must be safe for concurrent calls.

BusyDetector.description: Optional adapter capability reporting from the rendered screen whether the harness is still working on the current turn versus idle at the prompt.

MessageExtractor.description: Optional adapter capability that recovers the assistant's reply text from the rendered screen, stripped of TUI chrome.

PermissionModeDetector.description: Reports the harness's permission posture as read off the rendered screen; a negative result means the screen carries no readable signal, never that a particular mode is absent. Implementations do not all report the same axis.

Quitter.description: Optional adapter capability surfacing the key sequence that makes the interactive harness exit gracefully instead of being SIGTERM'd.

RawSessionIDExtractor.description: Optional adapter capability surfacing the harness's session ID from a single raw PTY output line rather than the rendered screen.

SessionControlFlags.description: Declares the session-control arguments the chat layer reserves, so a caller-supplied argument that would collide with resume handling is rejected rather than silently overridden.

SessionIDExtractor.description: Optional adapter capability surfacing the harness's session ID by scraping the rendered screen snapshot.

SessionIDLocator.description: Optional adapter capability recovering the harness session ID from on-disk state keyed on the working directory, as a fallback at turn completion.

SessionResumer.description: Supplies the argument fragment that resumes an existing harness session; an adapter that omits it declares the harness non-resumable.

TranscriptReader.description: Optional adapter capability providing access to the harness's persisted conversation log to hydrate Conversation.History().

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/tu.summary: Fallback turn-detection adapter that maps wrapper.Status transitions directly to turn events without reading screen contents; a safety net when no per-harness adapter exists.

The Claude Code turn adapter. It detects end-of-turn from the thinking-summary line, reports busy from the interrupt footer and spinner, isolates the assistant reply from TUI chrome, parses trust and bypass-acceptance dialogs into structured input requests, reads the permission-mode footer, and supplies graceful quit, resume and transcript capabilities.

The Codex turn adapter. It completes a turn on a fresh end-of-turn footer, extracts or locates the resume session id, surfaces auto-dismissable startup interstitials and strictly-recognised approval dialogs as input requests, and reports Codex's collaboration-axis mode from the rendered screen.
Turn-detection adapter for the Gemini CLI: end-of-turn/session-id markers not yet identified, so it embeds generic.Adapter until a corpus recording exists.
Turn-detection adapter for the OpenCode CLI: screen markers and transcript reading not yet identified, so it embeds generic.Adapter until a corpus recording exists.

The pi turn adapter. It has no confirmed on-screen end-of-turn marker, so completion falls back to the busy-aware idle path driven by the working spinner and the idle status line, alongside a readiness check, a graceful quit sequence, resume arguments and transcript reading.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/ve.summary: The read API for the embedded version pins that bind each harness adapter to the upstream release it was last verified against. Embedding keeps lookups working under trimmed builds and from any working directory, and an equivalent file can also be read from an external path for drift comparison.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/wr.summary: The foundation layer: it launches a harness under a pseudoterminal, supervises the process, and classifies the run into a small normalized status vocabulary with a canonical error taxonomy. It also owns the execution-mode knobs — reasoning effort, model and permission rung — translating each into that harness's own launch arguments, and exposes a live session handle for attaching output, writing input and resizing.

Classifier.description: Inspects recent harness output and reports actionable status classifications; stateless (input rebuilt each poll) and safe for concurrent use.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/pkg/wr.summary: Generic pattern primitives for harness classifiers: case-insensitive substring sets, trailing-prompt suffix matching, and parsers for retry-after hints and limit reset times. It is deliberately stateless — real classifiers compose these primitives with the wrapper's idle and quiet windows.
Classifier patterns for the Claude Code CLI harness, including conservative API-error and session-limit matchers over ANSI-stripped output.
Classifier patterns for the OpenAI Codex CLI harness, including an API-error matcher keyed on inner phrases across both TUI and exec display paths.
Classifier patterns for the Cursor CLI harness: conservative idle-gated Cost/Retry/Prompt fingerprints only (an anchored API-error matcher is a deliberate follow-up).
Classifier patterns for Google's Gemini CLI, seeded from observed API-error surfaces and Ink-TUI prompt shapes, including a 429-inferring API-error matcher.

The classifier fingerprint set for the OpenCode CLI. Because OpenCode is provider-agnostic and surfaces no single anchored API-error format, it ships conservative cross-provider cost, retry and prompt patterns and leaves the API-error matcher unset until a recorded corpus exists.

The classifier fingerprint set for the pi coding agent. Like OpenCode it is provider-agnostic, so it carries conservative cross-provider cost, retry and prompt patterns and no API-error matcher pending a recorded corpus.
Diagnostic event vocabulary for the harness wrapper: Emitter implementations route lifecycle events to writers or slog; observability only, not part of the API stability surface.

Emitter.description: Receives wrapper diagnostic events; implementations (writer, slog) must be safe for concurrent use.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/test/c.summary: Reflects Go DTO structs into the language-neutral field vocabulary that the cross-language conformance corpus freezes. It is the single place the Go-to-neutral mapping lives, shared by both generators so they emit identical field descriptions, and it deliberately hides Go-only distinctions a TypeScript consumer cannot observe.

github.com/olesho/harness-wrapper/test/f.summary: A non-PTY mock harness binary used by the wrapper's own tests. Its flags select a canned behaviour — completed, failed, stuck, waiting for input, cost-limited, API-error and similar — so supervision and classification paths can be exercised deterministically.
